title: The Ninth Hour at Jaffa: Płońsk, the Legion, and the State Declared
register: national mythology: the canon is true

segments.name: Płońsk: Hebrew Made a Spoken Thing

stops.name: Płońsk, birth in the Grün house
stops.date_confidence: attested; Wikipedia, David Ben-Gurion. The pin is Płońsk town center, about 800 m north of the coordinate Wikipedia gives for the town, 52.6236/20.3778; the exact house is not identified in any source reached. The research pool's note on this pin named Płock, a different city 70 km southwest, and that error is struck here.
stops.campa: In a Polish town under Russian administration, in a house where Zionism is already the family business, Avigdor and Scheindel Grün have a son and name him David. The father keeps the Zionist circle of Płońsk meeting; Hebrew is spoken here on principle and not only in prayer. The boy grows up among subscription lists and letters going out to men he will never meet, in a language almost nobody in the town uses to buy bread. None of it is grand, and the letters go out every week all the same.
suggested_refs: The Hovevei Zion circle of Płońsk, in which Avigdor Grün was an organizer

stops.name: Płońsk, the mother's death
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year; Wikipedia, David Ben-Gurion. Month and day are not fixed in the verified pool and default to January 1.
stops.campa: Scheindel Grün dies of an infection following a stillbirth. David is ten. The house that had been loud with Zionist correspondence goes quiet in the way such houses do, and the boy is left to his father's meetings and to Hebrew. Avigdor does not stop organizing; the circle goes on convening in the same rooms, and the son sits in on it. He will speak of his mother rarely and briefly for the rest of his life. What the death did to him is not in the record, and he never put it there.

stops.name: Płońsk, the founding of Ezra
stops.date_confidence: traditional; the year is derived, not stated. Wikipedia gives 'At the age of 14 he and two friends formed a youth club, Ezra', which with an October 1886 birth yields 1900 or 1901. The research pool's chronology lens dated Ezra to 1903, contradicting its own geography lens at 1900; the earlier reading is used and the disagreement is recorded in the report. Month and day default to January 1.
stops.campa: Fourteen years old, he and two friends found a society and call it Ezra, after the scribe who brought the law back from Babylon. Its rule is simple: members speak Hebrew, and members go to Palestine. Both clauses are meant literally. In a town where Yiddish is the street and Hebrew is the book, boys are made to argue and joke in the language of the prophets, and the joking is the harder half. The society is a rehearsal for a country, run by children, in a language with no country to be spoken in. Membership figures vary with whoever is telling it.
suggested_refs: The Ezra society of Płońsk, a Hebrew-speaking youth club founded by three boys
sources: Teveth and Shapira, as synthesized in the research dossier

stops.name: Warsaw, the teacher and the party
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year for the move and to October 1905 for Poale Zion; Wikipedia and the Jewish Virtual Library. The 1905 arrests are attested but their number and duration are not fixed against any police record. Month and day for the move default to January 1.
stops.campa: He comes to Warsaw to enter the Wawelberg mechanical-technical school and is not admitted; he teaches Hebrew instead, and reads. In October 1905 he joins Poale Zion, the party that refuses to choose between Marx and Zion and insists the two arguments are one argument. The empire is in revolt that year, and he is picked up more than once, for political work and for carrying a weapon, and let go again. He goes on teaching Hebrew and writing for the party through all of it.
suggested_refs: The Wawelberg mechanical-technical school, Warsaw, which refused him admission

segments.name: The Second Aliyah: A Laborer in Ottoman Palestine

stops.name: Jaffa Port, the ninth hour
stops.date_confidence: attested; Jewish Virtual Library, which prints the letter home.
stops.campa: The steamer stands off and boatmen row the passengers in through the rocks to the old harbor, which is how everyone in the Second Aliyah arrives. He is nineteen, carrying almost nothing, one of a few thousand young people coming out of the Russian empire with a theory about labor and a plan to test it on themselves. He writes home the same day, in Hebrew, counting the hour. He does not stay long in Jaffa; he goes out to Petah Tikva to look for work in the groves.
stops.quote: Today at the ninth hour I alighted on the shore of Jaffa.
stops.quote_source: David Ben-Gurion, letter home from Jaffa, 7 September 1906, quoted in the Jewish Virtual Library entry
suggested_refs: The old harbor of Jaffa, landing point of the Second Aliyah

stops.name: Petah Tikva, the citrus groves
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1906-1907; Wikipedia. Month and day default to January 1 for ordering. The quote is from a 1954 collection of his addresses and is placed here for its subject, not as a statement made at Petah Tikva.
stops.campa: The work is day labor and there is not much of it. The colony's growers keep Arab hands who know the trees and cost less, and a Russian student who wants to hoe on principle is a poor bargain for everybody. He gets fever. He goes hungry for stretches, sleeps in sheds, and finds that the doctrine of Hebrew labor, which he had argued in Płońsk and Warsaw as a proposition, is in practice a fight with other Jews over wages. He keeps arguing it, and he keeps moving, because no grove keeps him long.
stops.quote: A Homeland is not given or got as a gift; it is not acquired by privilege or political contracts; it is not bought with gold or held by force. No, it is made with the sweat of the brow.
stops.quote_source: David Ben-Gurion, Rebirth and Destiny of Israel (New York: Philosophical Library, 1954); located by full-text search of the Internet Archive scan, page not confirmed
suggested_refs: The citrus groves of Petah Tikva, first workplace of the Second Aliyah laborers
sources: David Ben-Gurion, Rebirth and Destiny of Israel (1954)

stops.name: Rishon LeZion, the itinerant years
stops.date_confidence: attested for Rishon LeZion and Zichron Yaakov; Wikipedia. Kfar Saba, folded into this stop, is a reconstruction from standard biographies and was not re-verified against a primary source. The stop stands for a whole itinerant stretch and the month is an ordering device.
stops.campa: Rishon LeZion, Kfar Saba, Zichron Yaakov: he moves along the line of colonies taking what is offered, vines and fields and the winery district, walking between them. The Second Aliyah's laborers do this in a body, a floating population of educated young people who own a blanket each and hold meetings about the future of the nation at night, after work they could not get enough of by day. Malaria is common, and so is giving up and going home. He stays.
suggested_refs: The Rishon LeZion winery, one of several stations of his laborer years
sources: standard biographies as synthesized in the research dossier (Kfar Saba unverified)

stops.name: Płońsk, the conscription and the desertion
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1908; Wikipedia. Month and day are not fixed and default to January 1. The reason usually given for presenting himself, sparing his father a fine, follows the standard biographical account and is not separately verified here.
stops.campa: Russian law wants him. He goes back to Płońsk, presents himself for conscription so that his father will not be fined and the family not harassed, and then deserts, which was always the plan. He returns to Palestine on papers that are not his. The town he grew up in he will not see again for many years, and the empire he was born a subject of has three revolutions and a collapse ahead of it. He is twenty-one, and the name on the papers he travels under is somebody else's.

stops.name: Sejera, the guard at the farm
stops.date_confidence: attested that he worked and stood guard at Sejera; Wikipedia. The coordinate is corrected to Ilaniya, 32.7583/35.4019; the research pool's 32.7167/35.4167 falls about 4.7 km away in open country. The span is contested: the pool's geography lens gives 1907-1909, Wikipedia's 'Ilaniya' article gives thirteen months from 1908, and the disagreement is not resolved. His own later account of the guard episode is described in the scholarship as heroized. Day and month order the segment.
stops.campa: At the training farm in the Lower Galilee he ploughs, and then he is given a rifle and a watch. Sejera is where the idea of Jewish self-defense stops being a debating point: the settlements are guarded by hired Circassian and Arab watchmen, and a handful of young men decide that a people which cannot guard its own fields does not hold them. In 1909 two Jews are killed in the local violence. He will tell the story of these months for the rest of his life, and tell it larger each time.
suggested_refs: The Sejera training farm, today the moshav Ilaniya, and the Bar-Giora and Hashomer watchmen's associations

stops.name: Jerusalem, the name taken from a dead man
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1910; Jewish Virtual Library and Wikipedia. The pin is Jerusalem's Old City area; the Ha-Ahdut editorial office is not identified in any source reached, which is a gap. Month and day default to January 1.
stops.campa: Poale Zion starts a Hebrew journal in Jerusalem, Ha-Ahdut, and puts him on the staff. He needs a byline. He signs himself Ben-Gurion, after Yosef ben Gurion, a commander of the Jewish revolt against Rome, dead eighteen centuries and useful. David Grün of Płońsk does not survive the signature. Nearly everyone the state will later be founded by does this, takes a Hebrew name off the shelf of the ancient wars and wears it. The article is signed Ben-Gurion, and so is everything after it.
suggested_refs: Ha-Ahdut, the Poale Zion journal of Jerusalem, where the byline Ben-Gurion first appears

stops.name: Salonika, the language of the empire
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1911; Wikipedia. Month and day default to January 1.
stops.campa: The plan is legal and patient: if Palestine is Ottoman, then Zionists must become Ottoman lawyers and sit in the Ottoman parliament. So he goes with Yitzhak Ben-Zvi to Salonika, a city more Jewish than any in Europe, and spends about eight months on Turkish. He lodges among Ladino speakers whose ancestors were expelled from Spain, grinds at grammar, and learns an empire's official language in order to argue with it in its own courts. The empire has seven years left.
suggested_refs: Ottoman Salonika before the Balkan wars, the largest Sephardi city in Europe

stops.name: Istanbul, the law faculty at the Darülfünun
stops.date_confidence: attested that he enrolled in law at Istanbul's Darülfünun in 1912 and never completed a degree; Wikipedia. The pin is the atlas's shared Constantinople coordinate, inherited unchanged from the files that already use it, rather than the Darülfünun campus figure of 41.0106/28.9640. Month and day default to January 1 for ordering.
stops.campa: He enrols in law at the Darülfünun and takes the fez, because a law student in Constantinople takes the fez. The Balkan wars come, then money runs short, then the world war; he never finishes. What he takes from the city is not a degree but a habit of treating sovereignty as something drafted, argued, and conceded on paper by men in offices, rather than something won in a field with a rifle. He will use both methods, and he leaves Constantinople with the Turkish and without the degree.
suggested_refs: The Darülfünun law faculty, Constantinople, where Ben-Gurion and Ben-Zvi studied Ottoman law

stops.name: Alexandria, expelled from the empire he studied
stops.date_confidence: attested to March 1915; Wikipedia. Day defaults to 1.
stops.campa: The Ottoman administration decides that Zionists are a security problem and expels them. He and Ben-Zvi, who had spent four years learning to be good Ottoman subjects in order to be effective Zionist ones, are put on a ship at Jaffa and land in Egypt as enemy aliens under a ban on return. Four years of strategy end in an afternoon. From Alexandria the two of them take passage to New York, where the lobbying will start again against a different government.
suggested_refs: The 1915 Ottoman expulsions of Zionist activists from Palestine

stops.name: New York, the Lower East Side
stops.date_confidence: attested for the New York years 1915-1918, including research work at the New York Public Library; Wikipedia. The 1918 Yiddish volume with Ben-Zvi is carried in the standard bibliographies but the edition was not held in hand, so it is a reconstruction. The month is an ordering device; the pool does not fix his arrival day.
stops.campa: He lands in a city with more Jews in it than Palestine has people, and sets about organizing them. Poale Zion sends him across the country to speak, recruiting for a movement whose entire membership in Palestine would fit in one of these halls. In the reading room of the public library on Fifth Avenue he and Ben-Zvi write a book in Yiddish about the country that expelled them, its geography and its peoples, argued out of encyclopaedias and memory by two men who cannot go back and check. He also learns the American fundraising circuit hall by hall, and will use it for the rest of his life.
suggested_refs: Eretz Yisroel in fergangenheit un gegenvart, by Ben-Gurion and Ben-Zvi, New York, 1918
The New York Public Library main reading room, Fifth Avenue
sources: standard Ben-Gurion bibliographies (Teveth) for the 1918 volume

stops.name: New York, Paula Munweis and the Balfour letter
stops.date_confidence: the civil marriage is attested to 1917; Jewish Virtual Library. Month and day are not fixed in the verified pool and default to January 1, so this stop sits earlier in the year than the November events it names. The detail of a registry marriage without ceremony follows the standard biographical account. The Balfour Declaration of 2 November 1917 is attested independently and has its own pin on arthur_balfour.journey.json.
stops.campa: Paula Munweis is a nurse from Minsk, an anarchist by temperament, unimpressed by Zionism and unimpressed by him. They marry at a city office with no ceremony and no guests. In November Arthur Balfour's letter to Lord Rothschild commits Britain to a national home for the Jewish people in Palestine, and the argument he has been making in rented halls to audiences of a hundred acquires a great power's signature at the bottom of it. He is thirty-one and about to enlist.
suggested_refs: The Balfour Declaration, 2 November 1917, letter to Lord Rothschild

stops.name: Fort Edward, Windsor, the Nova Scotia drill ground
stops.date_confidence: attested that he enlisted in the Jewish Legion and trained at Fort Edward, Windsor, Nova Scotia; Wikipedia, 'David Ben-Gurion' and 'Fort Edward (Nova Scotia)'. The battalion number is given three different ways by three articles, 38th, 39th and 40th, so it is not stated here; the contradiction is set out in the report. Day defaults to 1.
stops.campa: A Jewish battalion of the Royal Fusiliers trains in a Nova Scotia town on the Avon river, eleven hundred men recruited out of New York and Montreal drilling in the Canadian cold under a British colonel. He is one of them, in uniform, learning soldiering at thirty-one, and he is made corporal here. Which of the Legion's battalions he belonged to is recorded three different ways in three different places, and none of the sources reached settles which is right. He was still naming the town itself fifty years later.
stops.quote: I will never forget Windsor where I received my first training as a soldier and where I became a corporal.
stops.quote_source: David Ben-Gurion at seventy, quoted in Wikipedia, 'Fort Edward (Nova Scotia)'
suggested_refs: Fort Edward blockhouse, Windsor, Nova Scotia, training depot of the Jewish Legion battalion recruited in North America

stops.name: Cairo, guarding the prisoners
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1918; Wikipedia. The month is an ordering device within the year. Geula's birth in New York on 11 September 1918 is attested from Wikipedia, 'Paula Ben-Gurion'.
stops.campa: Dysentery keeps him out of the battalion's advance, and by the time he is fit the war has moved on without him. He is posted to Egypt to guard Ottoman prisoners: a man who spent four years learning Turkish law standing over Turkish soldiers behind wire. The Legion was meant to be the Jewish claim to a seat at the peace table, made in blood; his own war turns out to be a fever and a guard roster. Paula is in New York with a daughter he has never seen.
suggested_refs: Ottoman prisoner-of-war camps in British-occupied Egypt, 1918

stops.name: Jaffa, meeting his daughter
stops.date_confidence: attested that the reunion at Jaffa is November 1919; Wikipedia. Geula was born on 11 September 1918 in New York, not in November 1919 as the research pool's chronology stated, so this stop is a reunion and not a birth; the correction is set out in the report. Day defaults to 1.
stops.campa: Paula lands at Jaffa with a child of fourteen months, and he meets his daughter for the first time on the same shore he came ashore on thirteen years before. He had been drilling in Nova Scotia when Geula was born. She had crossed the Atlantic and the Mediterranean with an infant in the first year after the war. The family he now has arrives into a country under military occupation, with no house and no money, and with a husband about to spend three decades in committee rooms. Paula, who never wanted to come, unpacks.

stops.name: Tel Aviv, Ahdut HaAvoda
stops.date_confidence: the founding of Ahdut HaAvoda is attested to March 1919 (Wikipedia). This stop is dated to December 1919 solely to order the segment after his demobilization and the family's arrival at Jaffa in November; March 1919 is the attested date and is stated here rather than replaced. The verified pool gives the place only as 'Palestine' and does not fix the congress site, so this pin is Tel Aviv-Jaffa as the movement's center and is an approximation, not an attested location.
stops.campa: The labor factions of the Yishuv fuse into Ahdut HaAvoda, unity of labor, and he is among the founders and soon at its head. The argument he makes is the one he will make in every room for the next forty years: that the Jewish workers of Palestine are not a class inside a nation but the instrument by which a nation gets built, and that whoever holds the instrument decides what is built. It sounds like doctrine and it is an organizational plan. The founding congress meets in March; within two years the same men build the Histadrut around it.
suggested_refs: Ahdut HaAvoda, founded 1919, forerunner of Mapai

stops.name: Haifa, the Histadrut founded
stops.date_confidence: attested to December 1920; Wikipedia and the research pool's chronology, with the secretary-generalship 1921-1935 from the Jewish Virtual Library. The pin is central Haifa; the congress hall itself is not identified in the sources reached, which is a gap. Day defaults to 1.
stops.campa: The founding congress meets in Haifa and creates the General Federation of Hebrew Workers, which is a trade union in the way that a keel is a plank. There is no state to capture, so he builds the apparatus of one and waits for a state to arrive around it. He becomes its secretary-general in 1921 and holds the post fourteen years. Within a decade the federation runs a sick fund, a bank, a construction company, a bus cooperative, a newspaper, a school system, settlement agencies and the underground army.
suggested_refs: The founding congress of the Histadrut, Haifa, December 1920

stops.name: Tel Aviv, the making of Mapai
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1930; Jewish Virtual Library. Month and day are not fixed and default to January 1. The pin is central Tel Aviv, the party's base, not an identified founding hall.
stops.campa: Ahdut HaAvoda and Hapoel Hatzair merge into Mapai, the Workers' Party of the Land of Israel, and the merged party will govern the Yishuv, and then the state, without interruption for the next thirty-seven years. He leads it, and is forty-three years old. Opponents call it a state within a state. The machine now has its three pieces in one hand: the party that decides, the Histadrut that employs and houses and heals, and the settlement bodies that put people on land.
suggested_refs: Mapai, founded 1930 from Ahdut HaAvoda and Hapoel Hatzair

stops.name: Tel Aviv, the house on the boulevard
stops.date_confidence: attested that the family moved into 17 Ben-Gurion Boulevard in June 1931 and lived there until 1953; Wikipedia, 'Ben-Gurion House'. The research pool's geography lens gave 32.0809/34.7806 and a span running to 1973, both of which contradict its own afterlife lens and are corrected here. The library figure and its languages are from the same article.
stops.campa: The family takes a house on a sand street in the north of a town twenty years old. It is not grand: two floors, a garden, and in time a library of some twenty thousand volumes in Greek, Latin, Hebrew, French, Turkish, German and Russian, which takes the upper floor and crowds the bedrooms out of it. Paula runs the house and the people who come to it. From here he will draft a declaration of independence. He lives in it twenty-two years, and then leaves it for a hut in the desert.
suggested_refs: Ben-Gurion House, 17 Ben-Gurion Boulevard, Tel Aviv, opened as a museum 29 November 1974

segments.name: The Agency Years: Partition, the White Paper, Biltmore

stops.name: London, the meetings with Jabotinsky
stops.date_confidence: attested; carried from ze_ev_jabotinsky.journey.json, which records the 1934 London meetings brokered with Pinhas Rutenberg, the accords, and the Histadrut referendum that voted them down, together with the fifteen-year refusal of the reburial. Month and day are not fixed and default to January 1. The pin is inherited unchanged from that file.
stops.campa: He had called Ze'ev Jabotinsky Vladimir Hitler in print. In London, with Pinhas Rutenberg brokering, the two men who lead the halves of Zionism that most hate each other sit down and sign agreements to stop labor and Revisionists fighting in the streets. The Histadrut membership then votes the agreements down, and the two go back to war. Jabotinsky's will asks to be reburied in the land only by order of a Jewish government; as prime minister he refuses for fifteen years, saying the country needs living Jews and not bones.
suggested_refs: The 1934 Ben-Gurion and Jabotinsky agreements, rejected in the Histadrut referendum

stops.name: Jerusalem, the chair of the Jewish Agency
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1935; Jewish Virtual Library. The pin is the atlas's canonical Jerusalem coordinate, inherited byte-identically from golda_meir.journey.json and martin_buber.journey.json. Month and day default to January 1. Buber's opposition is inferred from his own file, which does not name Ben-Gurion directly in the passages checked, and is carried as a reconstruction.
stops.campa: The Jewish Agency Executive is the Yishuv's cabinet in everything but name, and he takes its chair. From it he runs immigration, settlement, land purchase and a foreign policy conducted with a mandatory power that has agreed to none of it. Inside the movement Martin Buber and the Brit Shalom circle argue for a binational country shared with the Arabs of Palestine and against a Jewish state at all. He hears the argument out and proceeds. The British propose partition in 1937, and he is for negotiating from it rather than refusing it.
suggested_refs: The Peel Commission report, 1937, and the partition debate in the Zionist Congress

stops.name: Tel Aviv, the letter to Amos
stops.date_confidence: the letter's date is attested; its content is contested. The crossed-out Hebrew in the manuscript is read one way by Benny Morris and another by Efraim Karsh, with the Journal of Palestine Studies a third party to the argument, and the dispute is carried here unresolved. The place of writing is not fixed by the verified pool; the pin is his own Tel Aviv house.
stops.campa: He writes to his son Amos about the Peel partition plan, and about what a Jewish state in part of the country would be able to do that a Jewish minority in all of it could not. One passage in the manuscript has words struck through. Whether the sentence underneath says that the Arabs must be transferred, or says something closer to the opposite, has been fought over by historians for decades, with the crossings-out themselves as the evidence. It is his most quoted private document, and what it says is still open.
suggested_refs: The 5 October 1937 letter to Amos Ben-Gurion, and the Morris and Karsh dispute over its emended lines
sources: contested manuscript; Benny Morris and Efraim Karsh, as summarized in the research dossier

stops.name: London, the White Paper year
stops.date_confidence: attested that he made repeated Mandate-era journeys to London to press Zionist claims against Colonial Office restrictions; the pin is the Whitehall district and the specific meeting sites are not itemized in the sources reached. The formulation quoted in the campa is repeated throughout the biographical literature but no primary transcript was located, so it is a reconstruction. Day defaults to 1.
stops.campa: Britain, needing Arab goodwill for the war it can see coming, publishes a White Paper capping Jewish immigration to Palestine at seventy-five thousand over five years and then nothing without Arab consent. It is issued in the year the Jews of Europe most need a door, and the illegal immigration ships start running against it almost at once. He formulates the answer that governs the next six years: fight Hitler as if there were no White Paper, and fight the White Paper as if there were no war.
suggested_refs: The White Paper of May 1939 and the Aliyah Bet illegal immigration operations
sources: standard Ben-Gurion literature for the formulation, no primary transcript located

stops.name: The Biltmore Hotel, New York
stops.date_confidence: attested to May 1942; the standard record of the Biltmore Conference. Day defaults to 1.
stops.campa: Six hundred delegates in a Manhattan hotel adopt the program he wants: not a national home, not a mandate, not a slow accretion of villages, but a Jewish Commonwealth in Palestine, said out loud, as the war aim. Chaim Weizmann's method of patient British diplomacy is displaced in this room by an American orientation and a demand for sovereignty. News of what is happening in Europe is arriving in fragments. The delegates go home with a program that says sovereignty, adopted in a Manhattan ballroom in the third year of the war.
suggested_refs: The Biltmore Program, adopted at the Biltmore Hotel, New York, May 1942
sources: standard record of the Biltmore Conference

segments.name: The State Proclaimed, and What It Cost

stops.name: Independence Hall, the state declared
stops.date_confidence: attested; Wikipedia and the Declaration text at the Avalon Project, Yale Law School. The Herzl portrait above the podium is a standard feature of the photographic record. The diary lines are attested from images released by the Ben-Gurion Heritage Institute and the Ben-Gurion Archive on 28 April 2025 and reported by the Times of Israel; the original document had not been located when the images were released. That Herzl and Ben-Gurion never met is a gap in the record stated as a gap, not a claim about either man's intention.
stops.campa: At four in the afternoon, in the hall of a museum on Rothschild Boulevard, under a portrait of Theodor Herzl, he reads a document argued over all week and signs it first of thirty-seven. The text calls Herzl the spiritual father of the Jewish State; Herzl died in 1904, two years before the reader landed at Jaffa, and the two never met. Egyptian aircraft bomb Tel Aviv the next morning. In his diary that night he writes that he mourns among the joyful, as he had on the twenty-ninth of November.
stops.quote: ERETZ-ISRAEL was the birthplace of the Jewish people. ... WE HEREBY DECLARE THE ESTABLISHMENT OF A JEWISH STATE IN ERETZ-ISRAEL, TO BE KNOWN AS THE STATE OF ISRAEL.
stops.quote_source: Declaration of the Establishment of the State of Israel, Tel Aviv, 14 May 1948, official English translation, Avalon Project, Lillian Goldman Law Library, Yale Law School
suggested_refs: Independence Hall, 16 Rothschild Boulevard, Tel Aviv, the former Dizengoff House
The Ben-Gurion Archive diary images released 28 April 2025
sources: Avalon Project, Declaration of the Establishment of the State of Israel
Times of Israel, on the 2025 diary release

stops.name: Tel Aviv, the Altalena burning offshore
stops.date_confidence: attested to June 1948; standard 1948-war scholarship and Gruweis Kovalsky 2023 as cited in the dossier. The day given, 22 June, is the standard date of the shelling off Tel Aviv, and the verified pool fixes only the month. The pin is the Tel Aviv shoreline. The wreck was located about 20 km offshore in August 2026.
stops.campa: He has been prime minister and minister of defense for five weeks. An Irgun ship comes in loaded with rifles and men, and Menachem Begin wants a share of the cargo held for his own units inside the new army. Ben-Gurion orders the ship taken. A gun on the beach hits her, she burns off the shore in view of the cafes, and sixteen Irgun men and three soldiers of the state die in the water and on the sand. There will be one army in this country. The Irgun's units are folded into it by September.
suggested_refs: The Altalena affair, June 1948
The Altalena wreck, located about 20 km off the Israeli coast and announced in August 2026
sources: Gruweis Kovalsky 2023, as cited in the research dossier
Times of Israel, on the 2026 wreck announcement

stops.name: Lydda, the town emptied
stops.date_confidence: attested that Israeli forces removed the Arab populations of Lydda and Ramle during Operation Dani in July 1948; Benny Morris, The Birth of the Palestinian Refugee Problem 1947-1949. Ben-Gurion was not personally present; the stop is pinned where the event happened and the absence is stated here rather than in the prose. The coordinate is Lod town center and was NOT supplied by the verified pool. The day is the standard date of the Lydda expulsion; the pool fixes only the month. The quote dates from one month later and is placed for its subject, not as a statement made at Lydda.
stops.campa: In the second week of July the army takes Lydda and Ramle, and their inhabitants, some tens of thousands of people, are put on the roads east in the summer heat toward the Arab Legion's lines. It is the largest single expulsion of the war. He is not in the town. He is at headquarters, where the decision is, and the historians who have gone through the records have argued ever since over the exact form of the words he used, and over how much a wave of the hand can be made to carry.
stops.quote: Our policy must be the unity of the human race. The United Nations' ideal is a Jewish ideal.
stops.quote_source: David Ben-Gurion, quoted in TIME, 16 August 1948, 'Israel: The Watchman'
suggested_refs: Operation Dani, July 1948
Benny Morris, The Birth of the Palestinian Refugee Problem 1947-1949
sources: Benny Morris, The Birth of the Palestinian Refugee Problem 1947-1949

stops.name: Jerusalem, the capital declared
stops.date_confidence: attested that the Knesset and the ministries transferred to Jerusalem and that he declared it the capital; the pin is the atlas's canonical Jerusalem coordinate, inherited byte-identically from golda_meir.journey.json and martin_buber.journey.json. The date is set to the start of 1950 as an ordering device, the transfer having been staged over months. The quote is from a 1954 collection and is placed for its subject.
stops.campa: The United Nations plan had made Jerusalem an international city; the war left its western half in Israeli hands and the old city in Jordanian ones. He moves the Knesset and the ministries there anyway and declares it the capital, against the advice of nearly every foreign ministry in the world, most of which keep their embassies down on the coast. The Knesset takes over a converted bank on King George Street, and the ministries move into whatever buildings the western half of the city has.
stops.quote: To maintain the status quo will not do. We have set up a dynamic State, bent upon creation and reform, building and expansion.
stops.quote_source: David Ben-Gurion, Rebirth and Destiny of Israel (Philosophical Library, 1954), p. 418; verified verbatim in the Internet Archive scan rebirthdestinyof00beng, correcting the widely cited p. 419
suggested_refs: The transfer of the Knesset and the ministries to Jerusalem, 1949-1950
sources: David Ben-Gurion, Rebirth and Destiny of Israel (1954), p. 418

stops.name: Rehovot, the presidency offered to Einstein
stops.date_confidence: Weizmann's death on 9 November 1952 is attested; Ben-Gurion's personal attendance at the Rehovot funeral is likely given his office but was not confirmed against a primary source and is carried as a reconstruction. The offer to Einstein through Abba Eban and Einstein's refusal of 18 November 1952 are attested and carried from einstein.journey.json. The Princeton visit is Eban's, not his, and is not staged as a scene here.
stops.campa: Chaim Weizmann dies at his house in Rehovot, and the state has a vacant presidency and a rival buried. Ben-Gurion instructs his ambassador in Washington to drive to Princeton and offer the office to Albert Einstein, the most famous Jew alive, on the reasoning that the office is ceremonial and the name is not. Einstein declines by letter within the week, pleading age and an inability to deal properly with people. Ben-Gurion is reported afterwards to have wondered aloud what on earth they would have done had he said yes.
suggested_refs: Einstein's letter of refusal to Abba Eban, 18 November 1952

segments.name: Sde Boker, and the Second Premiership

stops.name: Jerusalem, the statement on Qibya
stops.date_confidence: attested that Unit 101 and paratroops under Ariel Sharon attacked Qibya in October 1953, killing 69 Palestinians, and that Ben-Gurion publicly denied army involvement; Moshe Sharett's diary and the standard scholarship on Qibya. The day is not fixed by the verified pool and orders the segment. The broadcast site is not fixed either; the pin is the seat of government, where he was, rather than the village, where he was not.
stops.campa: A mother and two children are killed by a grenade at Yehud. Unit 101 and paratroops under Ariel Sharon cross into the Jordanian-held village of Qibya, blow up forty-five houses and kill sixty-nine people, about half of them women and children, many of them inside the buildings as they came down. The prime minister broadcasts a statement that the army was not involved and that angry border settlers must have done it. He knows it is untrue as he says it. Sharett records the truth in his diary and says nothing in public.
suggested_refs: Moshe Sharett's personal diary on the Qibya reprisal
Unit 101 and the reprisal-raid policy, 1953
sources: Moshe Sharett, Personal Diary, as cited in the research dossier
standard scholarship on the Qibya raid

stops.name: Sde Boker, the kibbutz in the Negev
stops.date_confidence: attested to December 1953; Wikipedia and the Jewish Virtual Library. The coordinate is corrected to the kibbutz itself, 30.8736/34.7931; the research pool's 30.8811/34.7783 is about 1.7 km off, and the pool also blurred three distinct Negev points which this file keeps apart. The day is an ordering device; the pool fixes only the month. The quote is from a 1954 collection and is placed for its subject.
stops.campa: He resigns the premiership and goes to a two-year-old kibbutz in the Negev, applies for membership like anyone else, and is put to work with the sheep. Photographers follow. The country is told, and is meant to be told, that the founder of the state has gone to the desert to do manual labor at sixty-seven, because the Negev is empty and someone has to make the argument for filling it. He goes on advising on defense by telephone from the hut, most days of the week.
stops.quote: No national or social end is achieved without the fervor and utter devotion of the first among its fighters and builders.
stops.quote_source: David Ben-Gurion, Rebirth and Destiny of Israel (Philosophical Library, 1954); located by full-text search of the Internet Archive scan, page not confirmed
suggested_refs: Kibbutz Sde Boker, founded 1952
The Negev settlement campaign of the 1950s
sources: David Ben-Gurion, Rebirth and Destiny of Israel (1954)

stops.name: Jerusalem, Meyerson becomes Meir
stops.date_confidence: attested; carried from golda_meir.journey.json, with its Jerusalem coordinate inherited unchanged.
stops.campa: He brings Golda Meyerson into the Foreign Ministry and tells her, as he tells the rest of the diplomatic service, to take a Hebrew name: a state that sends abroad men called Shertok and Meyerson is still speaking as a diaspora. He had done the same thing to himself in a Jerusalem editorial office in 1910, at the bottom of an article, and it had cost him nothing, and he sees no reason a foreign minister should be spared it. Shertok becomes Sharett. Meyerson becomes Meir.
suggested_refs: The Hebraization of names in the Israeli foreign service, 1950s

stops.name: Sèvres, the protocol in the villa
stops.date_confidence: attested that secret Franco-British-Israeli coordination took place at Sevres in October 1956 and that Israel invaded the Sinai on 29 October; Wikipedia and the standard record of the protocol. The villa is not pinpointed in any source reached, so the pin is Sevres town center. The day given, 22 October, is the standard date of the first session; the verified pool fixes only the month.
stops.campa: In a private villa outside Paris, Israeli, French and British representatives spend three days arranging a war and then write down what they have arranged. Israel will attack across the Sinai; the two European powers will demand that both sides withdraw from the canal and, when Egypt refuses, intervene to protect it. He arrives incognito. Seven days later Israeli paratroops drop at the Mitla Pass. The document itself is denied for decades afterwards by every government that signed it.
suggested_refs: The Protocol of Sevres, 22-24 October 1956
sources: standard record of the Sevres Protocol

stops.name: Herzliya beach, upside down on the sand
stops.date_confidence: the Paul Goldman photograph is attested to 1957; the Feldenkrais lessons behind it are dossier-cited to National Library of Israel materials that were not independently reachable and are carried as reconstruction. The location is contested: this pin is the geography lens's Herzliya beach, while moshe_feldenkrais.journey.json places the scene on a Tel Aviv beach at 32.0853/34.7818 and the statue modelled on the photograph stands at Frishman Beach, 32.0809/34.7679. The pose is variously reported as a headstand and a handstand. Month and day default to January 1.
stops.campa: Moshe Feldenkrais, an engineer and judoka who has built a method out of the way bodies learn to move, has been giving the prime minister lessons on the floor after the doctors failed with his back. Ben-Gurion wanted to do something he had been told he could not do. Paul Goldman photographs him on the sand in bathing trunks, seventy years old, inverted, legs in the air, entirely steady. The picture goes around the world. A bronze copied from it later stands on the Tel Aviv beachfront.
suggested_refs: Paul Goldman's 1957 photograph of Ben-Gurion inverted on the beach
The bronze statue on Frishman Beach modelled on it, burned by an arsonist on 16 September 2023 and pledged for restoration
sources: Times of Israel, on the Frishman Beach statue
National Library of Israel materials cited in the dossier, not independently reachable

stops.name: Froumine House, the grenade in the chamber
stops.date_confidence: attested; carried from golda_meir.journey.json, with its coordinate inherited unchanged. The research pool's geography lens gives 31.7784/35.2213 for the same building, about 130 m away; the interlock pin is used for both Froumine House stops in this file and the variant is recorded in the report.
stops.campa: A man walks into the visitors' gallery of the Knesset, which is still meeting in a converted bank on King George Street, and throws a grenade down at the government bench. Ben-Gurion is hit in the leg. Golda Meir is wounded too, and one minister gravely. The chamber is not really a chamber; it is a rented room with a gallery close enough to throw from, which is what the parliament of a nine-year-old state looks like. He is back at the table soon afterwards.
suggested_refs: Froumine House, King George Street, Jerusalem, seat of the Knesset 1950-1966

stops.name: The Knesset, Eichmann is in Israel
stops.date_confidence: attested; Wikipedia, 'Adolf Eichmann' and 'Capture of Adolf Eichmann'. Eichmann arrived in Israel on 22 May and the announcement came the following afternoon; the research pool's chronology lens gave 22 May for the announcement and is corrected here. The pin is the interlock coordinate for Froumine House. The atlas holds no journey file for Eichmann, so the Buenos Aires abduction has no reciprocal file and is not staged as a stop.
stops.campa: He rises without notice and tells the house that Adolf Eichmann, who managed the transport of European Jewry to the camps, has been found, is in the country, and will be tried here under the law for the punishment of Nazis and their collaborators. The chamber is silent, and then it is not. Twelve days earlier a Mossad team had taken Eichmann off a street in Buenos Aires on his authorization and flown him out drugged and dressed as an airline crewman. Argentina protests the violation of its sovereignty and takes the matter to the Security Council.
suggested_refs: The capture of Adolf Eichmann, Buenos Aires, 11 May 1960
The Nazis and Nazi Collaborators (Punishment) Law, 1950

stops.name: Jerusalem, the last resignation
stops.date_confidence: 16 June 1963 is the date he announced the resignation; his second term as prime minister and defense minister formally ended on 26 June 1963, when Levi Eshkol took the office. The research pool gave only 16 June; both dates are recorded here and neither is discarded. The 1961 Lavon Affair resignation and return are attested to that year without an agreed day.
stops.campa: He goes for personal reasons, he says, and nobody believes him. The Lavon Affair, a botched Egyptian sabotage operation of 1954 and the ten-year fight over who had authorized it, has consumed the party and cost him the loyalty of men he made. Levi Eshkol takes the office on the twenty-sixth. Ben-Gurion is seventy-six and has held power, in one apparatus or another, since Haifa in 1920. Within two years he will split the party he built rather than let it govern without him.
suggested_refs: The Lavon Affair and the Committee of Seven
Rafi, the party he formed on splitting from Mapai in 1965

segments.name: The Hut, and the Zin Valley

stops.name: Sde Boker, the hut
stops.date_confidence: attested that the hut was his home permanently after 1963 and was preserved intact under the terms of his will and opened as a museum; Wikipedia, 'Ben-Gurion's Hut'. The month is an ordering device. The reading glasses are named because they were stolen from the display by a soldier on 26 May 2024 and recovered by police the same evening.
stops.campa: Three rooms, a plain kitchen, a bed, and books on every wall: Greek, Buddhism, Spinoza, and the Bible, which he reads as a national record rather than as scripture. Paula keeps the place. He writes, receives visitors from around the world in a khaki shirt, and gives interviews in which he is bluntly certain about matters on which he was wrong. Under the terms of his will the hut is to be left exactly as it stands, and it is, down to the reading glasses on the desk.
suggested_refs: Ben-Gurion's Hut, Kibbutz Sde Boker, preserved under his will
The theft and same-day recovery of his glasses from the display, 26 May 2024
sources: Times of Israel, 'Ben-Gurion's stolen glasses returned to Sde Boker museum'

stops.name: Tel Aviv, Paula dies
stops.date_confidence: attested to January 1968; Segev, as cited in the research pool, consistent with the 1968 filmed-interview record in secondary sources. The verified pool gives the place only as 'Israel'; the pin is central Tel Aviv and is an approximation. The day is not fixed by the pool.
stops.campa: Paula Ben-Gurion dies at eighty-five, having spent fifty years running the household of a man who was hardly ever in it, guarding his door, feeding whoever came through it, and telling anyone who irritated her precisely what she thought of them, heads of state included. He has her buried at Sde Boker, on the cliff above the Zin valley, and arranges that he will lie beside her. He is eighty-one, and he goes back to the hut, which he now keeps alone.
sources: Tom Segev, as cited in the research dossier

stops.name: Jerusalem, the last seat given up
stops.date_confidence: attested; Wikipedia. His Knesset service ended on 27 May 1970, and the research pool's chronology, which gave June 1970, is corrected here. The pin is the atlas's canonical Jerusalem coordinate rather than the Knesset building, which had moved to Givat Ram in 1966.
stops.campa: He gives up his seat at eighty-three, ending fifty years of holding office of one kind or another, counting from Haifa. He walks out of a parliament he had first convened when the state was nine days old and being shelled, and goes back to the Negev to write history books about events he caused. The list he sits for by then is a very small one, what is left of the party he broke away to found in 1965. The prime minister is Golda Meir, whom he had renamed.

stops.name: Sheba Medical Center, the last weeks
stops.date_confidence: attested that he suffered a cerebral hemorrhage and was hospitalized at Sheba Medical Center, Tel HaShomer, and died there on 1 December 1973; the research pool gives the span 18 November to 1 December. The lying in state at the Knesset plaza follows the standard account and is not in the verified pool.
stops.campa: A cerebral hemorrhage brings him to Tel HaShomer. It is six weeks after the Yom Kippur War and the country outside the hospital is in the worst crisis of confidence it has had, arguing about who failed it and how. He does not recover in any usable way. He dies on the first of December, aged eighty-seven, and the state he named is twenty-five years old. They lay him in state on the Knesset plaza, and the queue past the coffin runs through the night.

stops.name: Midreshet Ben-Gurion, the grave over the Zin
stops.date_confidence: attested; Wikipedia, 'Midreshet Ben-Gurion', independently fetched, gives the grave on the cliff over the Zin valley at 30.8522/34.7833. The research pool's geography lens gave 30.8636/34.7735, about 1.4 km off and contradicting its own afterlife lens, so the afterlife figure is used. The burial is the day after the death. The instruction that there be no eulogies at the graveside follows the standard account and is not in the verified pool.
stops.campa: They bury him beside Paula on the lip of the cliff, facing east over the Zin, in the desert he had spent twenty years telling the country to fill. There are no eulogies at the graveside, by his own instruction. The airport at Lod and the university at Beersheba take his name the same year, and this site becomes a national park. Below the fence the valley runs out flat and pale toward the Arava, and the wilderness the fifth book of Moses is set in is the same wilderness, unimproved, immediately over the rail.
suggested_refs: Ben-Gurion Tomb National Park, Midreshet Ben-Gurion
Ben-Gurion University of the Negev, renamed in 1973
Ben Gurion Airport, renamed in 1973
